study.notes: STUDY: randomised open label mechanistic trial (NCT01740921, Exeter) of liraglutide vs diet induced weight loss in overweight or obese adults with type 2 diabetes on metformin; 30 randomised 1 to 3 to diet or liraglutide, 22 completed 16 weeks and attended both assessments (diet 7, liraglutide 15), completers analysed; liraglutide 0.6 mg daily for 2 weeks then 1.2 mg daily to week 16 (dose_mg 1.2); the primary interest of the paper is adipose tissue biopsy expression, the circulating and clinical markers of Table 1 are supporting measurements (prespecified_endpoint FALSE); Table 1 gives mean plus or minus SD per arm at baseline and after 4 months (route arm_change_imputed_r, correlation 0.5; asterisks are within arm Wilcoxon tests, not used), the HbA1c change is printed per arm with SD in the text (route arm_sds, between group p 0.62); fasting insulin from paired subsets (diet 7, liraglutide 13, two haemolysed) and VAT and SCAT areas by MRI from paired subsets (diet 3, liraglutide 10), row level n; pct_weight_change from the Table 1 means in the liraglutide arm, 89.48 to 87.09 kg, minus 2.39 kg equals minus 2.7 percent (diet 97.61 to 91.54 kg, minus 6.2 percent; the paper reports the between group difference in weight change as significant by Mann Whitney, no contrast printed); medication reductions in the liraglutide arm (three stopped metformin, two reduced it, two stopped gliclazide); funded by the EFSD GSK programme grant and NIHR Exeter infrastructure, no known conflicts declared, liraglutide manufacturer not involved (industry_funded FALSE, see doubts); rob_overall high

rows.notes: Results text: change in HbA1c minus 0.72 plus or minus 0.65 percent liraglutide vs minus 0.50 plus or minus 0.43 percent diet, P 0.62 between groups; baselines from Table 1 (7.43 and 7.34)
Table 1: fasting glucose mmol/l, baseline and after 4 months per arm
Table 1 footnote a: paired subset, diet n 7, liraglutide n 13 (two haemolysed)
Table 1: hs-CRP mg/l by ELISA, baseline and after 4 months per arm
Table 1: systolic BP mmHg; within arm p 0.013 in the liraglutide arm
Table 1: heart rate bpm (the diet arm fell by about 10 bpm, the liraglutide arm was unchanged)
Table 1 footnote b: VAT area cm2 by MRI in paired subsets, diet n 3, liraglutide n 10; within arm p below 0.05 in the liraglutide arm

json.design: randomised open label mechanistic trial, liraglutide 1.2 mg vs diet induced weight loss, type 2 diabetes with overweight or obesity, 30 randomised 1 to 3, 22 completers analysed (15 and 7), 16 weeks
json.reason: full text group (institutional route); nine inventory markers from Table 1 and the results text (HbA1c change with SD per arm by the arm_sds route, the others by the imputed change route)
other_markers: weight, BMI, waist and hip measures
subcutaneous adipose tissue area by MRI
circulating adiponectin (reported only for the liraglutide weight losers subgroup)

rob.justification: randomised 1 to 3 without a described sequence or concealment (D1 some concerns); open label with glucose lowering medication reduced in the liraglutide arm only and a behavioural comparator (D2 high); 30 randomised, 22 completers analysed with no account of the 8 dropouts in the text, MRI and insulin in smaller paired subsets (D3 high); laboratory assays, unblinded pressure and heart rate measurement (D4 some concerns); registered trial but the circulating markers are supporting outcomes of a biopsy study without a stated analysis plan (D5 some concerns)

doubts: very small diet arm (7; VAT subset 3)
industry_funded recorded FALSE: the EFSD GSK programme is an industry funded academic grant scheme not involving the manufacturer of liraglutide; the verifier may prefer TRUE
comparator is an active weight loss intervention; the diet arm lost more weight than the liraglutide arm, so contrasts are not drug vs no treatment
phase recorded 4 by convention for an investigator initiated trial of a marketed drug; not stated in the paper
